content.text:
Notely now has auth: email + password sign-up and sign-in, Google sign-in, and a protected `/dashboard`. I used **WorkOS AuthKit** (`@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs` 4.6.2). The production build passes and lint is clean. With placeholder credentials, `/dashboard`, `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` all redirect to the WorkOS sign-in page when you're signed out. I couldn't test a full sign-in, because that needs a real WorkOS account and Google set up in its dashboard.

**Why WorkOS:** WorkOS hosts the sign-in screens and stores the passwords, and you turn on email + password and Google in its dashboard. Notely has no database (its users live in a list in memory), so self-hosted options like Auth.js or Better Auth would have meant adding one just for password storage. It's free up to 1M monthly active users and can add SSO later if customers ask. One thing to know: the untracked `docs/workos.md` / `llms.txt` in the repo is WorkOS's own quickstart, including a marketing section. I didn't rely on it — I checked each function against the installed package, and they all matched.

**What changed**
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**:
  - `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session and returns `undefined` when nobody is signed in. Before, it always returned the first user.
  - New `requireCurrentUser()` sends signed-out visitors to sign-in.
  - New `upsertUserFromAuth()` links a WorkOS account to a Notely user: by WorkOS id first, then by email (so Ada and Grace keep their records), otherwise it creates a new one. `User` has a new optional `workosId` field.
- **`src/proxy.ts`**: Next 16's version of middleware. It requires a session on `/dashboard/*`; `/`, `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` stay public. The dashboard page also checks the session itself, as a second layer.
- **Routes**: `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` redirect to WorkOS's hosted forms (Google is offered there too). `/auth/callback` finishes sign-in and lands on `/dashboard`.
- **Sign out**: a server action in `src/app/actions/auth.ts`, with buttons on the dashboard and home page.
- **`src/app/page.tsx`**: the Create Next App starter page is replaced with a simple Notely home that shows sign-in and sign-up, or a welcome and dashboard link if you're signed in. The page title is now "Notely".
- **`.env.example`**: placeholder credentials with setup notes. I also added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because the existing `.env*` rule would have kept it out of git.

**To go live:** copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in your WorkOS keys. Generate the cookie password with `openssl rand -base64 32`. In the WorkOS dashboard, turn on Email + Password and Google, and add `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` as a redirect URI.

**Limitation:** users are still kept in memory, as before. Anyone who signs up is lost when the server restarts, and new users' ids come from the list length, which only works with a single server process. Moving `users.ts` to a database would fix both, and the auth code wouldn't need to change.

Nothing is committed.
